children: Climb Bio reported Phase 1 results for CLYM116 showing sustained APRIL suppression through 12 weeks and reductions in IgA and Gd-IgA1.
A single dose of at least 480 mg suppressed free APRIL by 90% or more through 12 weeks, supporting a potential every-12-week regimen.
At 12 weeks, an 800 mg dose reduced Gd-IgA1 by approximately 70% and IgA by approximately 60%.
CLYM116 had an estimated half-life of approximately 33 days, with consistent, linear exposure across the two Phase 1 studies.
The antibody was generally well tolerated; no serious adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities, or hypogammaglobulinemia were reported.
NAVIGATE-2 Phase 2 is enrolling patients, with initial data expected in the first half of 2027; a global Phase 3 trial is expected to begin in 2027, pending regulatory feedback.
